hypotheses.paper: théorème de Krein-Milman (Bourbaki EVT II § 4 th. 1), cited
hypotheses.note: Mathlib IsCompact.extremePoints_nonempty and closure_convexHull_extremePoints, applied to the compact convex section {v ∈ F(W) | ℓ v = 1}

findings: benzecri1960_ch3.tex:1571: the printed bound n ≥ 1 is necessary and sufficient: a point of S(0) is a convex body with a single facette (S0_lacks_two_singleton_facettes, deux_points_extremaux_iff). Not a defect of the paper: the bound is printed.

benzecri1960_ch3.tex:1575-1586: the proof's remark « facette réduite à un point = point extrémal » holds in both directions, over any real vector space, for any convex part k and any form ℓ > 0 on F(k), reading the extreme point in the affine chart ℓ = 1 (Sphere.facetteK_eq_singleton_iff_mem_extremePoints). Only one direction (extreme ⇒ one-point facette) is used by the proof.

benzecri1960_ch3.tex:1583-1586: « Il suffit d'appliquer … Krein-Milman » leaves implicit the step that the compact set has at least two extreme points; it holds because a convex body with one extreme point would be a single open point of S(n), impossible for n ≥ 1 (S(n) connected). This is where n ≥ 1 is used.

instances: Benzecri.TriangleInstance.triangle_three_facettes: the closed triangle of S(2) (rays of the positive octant of ℝ³) is a convex body whose three vertices are three pairwise distinct facettes reduced to a point; general form for the closed simplex of S(m): isCorpsConvexeS_simplexS, facetteK_vertex, isFacetteK_vertex, vertex_injective
kb_proposals: Chapter3/PointsExtremaux: read the affine chart of the open hemisphere ℓ > 0 as the section coneSection k ℓ = {v ∈ F k | ℓ v = 1} of the cone, not via instAddTorsorHemi: it is closed (isClosed_insert_zero_F ∩ ℓ⁻¹{1}), bounded (exists_mul_norm_le), convex, and Mathlib's Krein–Milman applies in ℝⁿ⁺¹ directly; facetteK_eq_singleton_iff_mem_extremePoints is the bridge one-point facette ⇔ extreme point.
To show a convex body of S(n), n ≥ 1, is not a point: interior W = {x} makes {x} clopen in the connected S(n) (connectedSpace_S), and −x ≠ x (Sphere.neg_ne_self).
